title: Other High-Value ISO Standards — 13485, 50001, 31000, 19011, and the 17000 Family
shortDescription: The next tier of standards worth knowing cold: medical devices, energy, risk, auditing, and conformity-assessment vocabulary.
genZNote: The standards that don't headline the syllabus but absolutely headline the answer key.

sections.heading: ISO 13485 — Medical Devices Quality Management
bullets: Full title: 'Medical devices — Quality management systems — Requirements for regulatory purposes.'
Specifies QMS requirements for organizations involved in the design, production, installation, and servicing of MEDICAL DEVICES specifically — not general products.
Structurally based on ISO 9001 but with medical-device-specific additions around risk management, regulatory compliance, and traceability of devices (crucial for recalls).
Certifiable — often a prerequisite for regulatory approval/market access for medical devices in many countries.
Do not confuse with ISO 15189 — ISO 13485 is about manufacturing/servicing the DEVICE; ISO 15189 is about running the LABORATORY that uses devices to test patient samples.

sections.heading: ISO 50001 — Energy Management Systems
bullets: Specifies requirements for an Energy Management System (EnMS), helping organizations systematically improve energy performance, efficiency, and consumption.
Uses the same High Level Structure/continual-improvement pattern as ISO 9001/14001/45001.
Distinct from ISO 14001: 14001 covers an organization's overall environmental impact broadly; 50001 focuses specifically and deeply on energy use and efficiency.

sections.heading: ISO 31000 — Risk Management Guidelines
bullets: Provides principles, framework, and a process for managing risk — applicable to any organization, any type of risk, any sector.
Important distinction: ISO 31000 is GUIDANCE, not a requirements standard — it is NOT certifiable, unlike ISO 9001/14001/45001/27001.
'Risk-based thinking', embedded across many other modern ISO management-system standards, draws conceptually on the principles ISO 31000 lays out.

sections.heading: ISO 19011 — Guidelines for Auditing Management Systems
bullets: Provides guidance on how to plan and conduct audits of management systems (quality, environmental, safety, etc.) — covering audit principles, programme management, and auditor competence.
Also GUIDANCE, not a certifiable requirements standard — organizations use it to design good internal (and sometimes external) audit practices, but you cannot be 'ISO 19011 certified'.

rows: Vocabulary and general principles of conformity assessment — the definitions used across this whole family.
Requirements for bodies performing INSPECTION (as distinct from testing or certification).
Requirements for bodies providing AUDIT AND CERTIFICATION of management systems (i.e. the requirements a certification body itself must meet).
Requirements for testing and calibration LABORATORIES (covered in its own topic in this subject).

sections.heading: ISO 10001 and ISO 10002 — Customer Satisfaction
bullets: ISO 10001 — guidelines for codes of conduct for customer satisfaction (setting clear, honest expectations upfront).
ISO 10002 — guidelines for complaints handling within organizations.
Both are guidance documents that support, but sit outside, the core ISO 9001 certifiable requirements.

sections.heading: Certifiable vs Guidance-Only — Quick Recap Across This Whole Topic
bullets: Certifiable (you CAN be certified against these): ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, ISO 22000, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO 15189, ISO/IEC 17025, ISO 13485, ISO 50001.
Guidance only (NOT certifiable): ISO 9000, ISO 9004, ISO 31000, ISO 19011, ISO 10001, ISO 10002.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Beyond the headline standards, ISO 13485 (medical devices), ISO 50001 (energy), ISO 31000 (risk guidance), ISO 19011 (audit guidance), and the ISO/IEC 17000 conformity-assessment family round out the high-value standards worth knowing.
keyFacts: ISO 13485: medical DEVICE manufacturing QMS — distinct from ISO 15189 (medical LABORATORY operation).
ISO 50001: energy management — narrower and deeper than ISO 14001's broad environmental scope.
ISO 31000 and ISO 19011 are GUIDANCE documents — neither is certifiable.
ISO/IEC 17020 = inspection bodies; ISO/IEC 17021 = certification bodies for management systems; ISO/IEC 17025 = testing/calibration labs — three different conformity-assessment actors.
commonConfusion: ISO 13485 (device manufacturing) and ISO 15189 (medical lab operation) are both 'medical' but govern completely different activities.
ISO 31000 and ISO 19011 are guidance, not certifiable requirements standards — unlike most other standards in this subject.

highYieldFacts: ISO 31000 (risk) and ISO 19011 (audit guidance) are NOT certifiable — a frequently tested exception to the 'you can be ISO certified' pattern.
ISO/IEC 17021 sets requirements for CERTIFICATION bodies themselves — i.e. the standard that governs the auditors of other standards.
ISO 13485 is structurally based on ISO 9001 but adds medical-device-specific regulatory and traceability requirements.
commonTraps: Do not say an organization is 'ISO 31000 certified' or 'ISO 19011 certified' — both are guidance documents only.
Do not confuse ISO/IEC 17020 (inspection bodies) with ISO/IEC 17025 (testing/calibration laboratories) — different conformity-assessment activities entirely.
mustRemember: ISO 50001 is about energy specifically, not general environmental impact (that's ISO 14001's job).
ISO 13485 vs ISO 15189: device manufacturing vs laboratory operation — do not merge them.
possibleQuestions: Which of these is NOT certifiable: ISO 9001 / ISO 31000 / ISO 14001 / ISO/IEC 27001?
